name: Hexadrine
manufacturer: Unnamed the Gray Zone chemist collective (the Cascade Labs)
description: Hexadrine is an unlicensed adrenal stack produced in rotating the Gray Zone laboratory locations by a distributed chemist network known only as the Cascade Labs. It combines six stimulant compounds — epinephrine analog, amphetamine derivative, synthetic cortisol blocker, crude SNT-reactive catalyst, vasoconstrictor, and a nootropic fragment — in a formulation that varies batch to batch because standardization requires resources the Cascade Labs don't have. When it works, it is brutally effective. When it doesn't, it causes cardiac arrest.
effects: Intense adrenal surge — stronger than corporate equivalents at peak
SNT-reactive catalyst causes augmentation interaction effects in chrome-heavy users
Cheap and accessible adrenal boost for unaugmented the Gray Zone combatants
side_effects: Cardiac arrest risk — estimated 3-8% per dose depending on batch purity
Severe hypertension causing hemorrhagic stroke in predisposed users
Unpredictable batch variation makes dosing unreliable
SNT catalyst can cause dangerous overclock in users with neural augments
Contamination risk — heavy metal traces documented in multiple batches
cultural_context: Hexadrine is what you take when you cannot afford anything better and you need to survive the next twenty minutes. It is the chemical reality of inequality in GLMZ — the Gray Zone's answer to Dravecor, produced without quality control, sold without warning labels, and used by people who have run the math and decided a 5% chance of dying from the drug is better than a 90% chance of dying from whoever is coming through the door. The Cascade Labs are an open secret; MCPD raids them periodically but new labs open within days.
story_hooks: A bad Hexadrine batch has killed seventeen people in a the Gray Zone district over one week — someone is deliberately adulterating the supply, and the Cascade Labs want a runner to find out who before they lose their market entirely.

The SNT-reactive catalyst in Hexadrine is causing augmented users to experience involuntary chrome activation — someone with high-end military augments took a dose of Hex and went completely out of control, and now three people are dead.

A Tier 3 journalist is investigating the Cascade Labs for a story on the Gray Zone pharmaceutical inequality — she has found something in the chemist collective's funding trail that suggests they are not as grassroots as they appear.
